question: What is the nerve supply of the diaphragm?
key_points: motor supply by the phrenic nerve (C3, C4, C5)
sensory to central part by phrenic nerve
peripheral part sensory by lower intercostal nerves (and subcostal)

question: What are the boundaries of the inguinal canal?
key_points: anterior: external oblique aponeurosis (plus internal oblique laterally)
posterior: transversalis fascia and conjoint tendon
roof: arching fibres of internal oblique and transversus abdominis
floor: inguinal ligament (and lacunar ligament)
deep ring and superficial ring as openings

question: Which nerve is injured in wrist drop and why?
key_points: radial nerve
injured in the radial groove / midshaft humerus fracture
paralysis of wrist and finger extensors

question: What is the blood supply of the head of the femur?
key_points: medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries (retinacular branches)
artery of the ligament of the head (obturator artery)
cruciate anastomosis / nutrient artery contribution

question: Which nerve roots are involved in Erb's palsy and what is the clinical picture?
key_points: C5 and C6 (upper trunk)
arm adducted and medially rotated, forearm extended and pronated (waiter's tip)
loss of abduction, lateral rotation and elbow flexion

question: What are the contents of the carotid sheath?
key_points: common and internal carotid artery
internal jugular vein
vagus nerve

question: Name the muscles of the rotator cuff.
key_points: supraspinatus
infraspinatus
teres minor
subscapularis

question: Describe the course and relations of the ureter.
key_points: descends on the psoas major, crosses pelvic brim at bifurcation of common iliac artery
in the pelvis passes to the bladder; in the female passes under the uterine artery ('water under the bridge')
in the male crossed by the vas deferens near the bladder
enters bladder obliquely at the trigone

question: What is the venous drainage of the rectum?
key_points: superior rectal vein to inferior mesenteric vein to portal system
middle and inferior rectal veins to internal iliac and internal pudendal to systemic system
portosystemic anastomosis at the anorectal junction

question: List the bronchopulmonary segments of the right lung.
key_points: upper lobe: apical, posterior, anterior
middle lobe: lateral, medial
lower lobe: superior (apical), medial basal, anterior basal, lateral basal, posterior basal
